deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The previous page treats the trinomial equation x^7 - 3x^4 - 6 = 0. It first finds the real root through y = x^3 (y ≈ 3.95825, so x ≈ 1.5819). It then finds one complex pair with φ ≈ 112°29'. This page finds the other two complex pairs by the same polar method.

THE METHOD (my statement of what the numbers imply). Put x = r(cos φ + i sin φ). The real and imaginary parts give:
- r^7 cos7φ - 3r^4 cos4φ = 6
- r^7 sin7φ - 3r^4 sin4φ = 0

Solving this as a linear system in r^7 and 3r^4 gives:
- r^7 = -6 sin4φ / sin3φ
- r^4 = -2 sin7φ / sin3φ
- hence r^3 = 3 sin4φ / sin7φ.

For a trial φ, Gauss computes 7 log r, 4 log r and 3 log r with 10-place logarithms and divides by 7, 4 and 3. The three values of log r agree only at a true root. Each logarithm carries a linear term in u, the correction to φ in arcseconds. The u-coefficient is d log10|sin kφ|/dφ'' = k·cot(kφ)·M·sin1'', expressed in units of 10^-5. Equating two of the three log r values gives u.

PART 1: φ = 47°45'19.1926481".

Multiples:
- 3φ = 143°15'57.5779443"
- 4φ = 191°1'16.7705924"
- 7φ = 334°17'14.3485367"

Interpolated log-sines:
- log sin3φ = log sin36°44'0" + 68333.7. The correction is 2.42216" × cot × M sin1".
- So log sin3φ = 9.77677 44636.7.
- log|sin4φ| = log sin11°1'20" - 349088.9 (3.2294"), giving 9.28142 95965.1.
- log|sin7φ| = log sin25°42'50" - 190133.3 (4.3485"), giving 9.63734 81149.7.

Auxiliary 7-place columns:
- 9.3233592 = log(M·sin1''·10^5) = log 0.210552.
- 0.1270915, 0.7104674 and 0.3173558 are log|cot 3φ|, log|cot 4φ| and log|cot 7φ|.
- Adding the constant gives 9.4504507, 0.0338266 and 9.6407150.
- Their antilogs are 0.2821309, 1.0810022 and 0.4372351.
- 0.3841841, 0.5091694 and 0.6383432 are the logs of the interpolation remainders 2.42216", 3.2294" and 4.3485".
- Multiplying the antilogs by k = 3, 4, 7 gives the u-coefficients 0.84639, 4.32401 and 3.06064.

Logarithms entering the solution:
- log(sin3φ/6) = 9.77677 44636.7 - log6 (0.77815 12503.8) = 8.99862 32132.9, with u-term -0.84639u.
- log|sin4φ| = 9.28142 95965.1, with u-term +4.32401u.
- log(|sin7φ|/3) = 9.16022 68602.5, with u-term -3.06064u.

Differences:
- 7 log r = 0.28280 63832.2 + 5.17040u
- 4 log r = 0.16160 36469.6 - 2.21425u
- 3 log r = 0.12120 27362.6 + 7.38465u

Dividing by 7, 4 and 3:
- 0.04040 09118.9 + 0.73863u
- ...117.4 - 0.55356u
- ...120.9 + 2.46155u

Result: u = -0.0000116". So φ = 47°45'19.1926365" (not written) and log r = 0.0404009119, i.e. r ≈ 1.09748.

PART 2: root with argument 180° - ψ, where ψ = 36°33'25.4075".

Sign relations: sin3φ = sin3ψ, sin4φ = -sin4ψ, sin7φ = sin7ψ. So r^7 = 6 sin4ψ/sin3ψ and r^4 = -2 sin7ψ/sin3ψ.

Multiples:
- 3ψ = 109°40'16.2225"
- 4ψ = 146°13'41.6300"
- 7ψ = 255°53'57.8525"

Interpolated log-sines:
- log sin3ψ = log sin70°19'40" + 28433.7 (3.7775"), giving 9.97388 49113.7.
- log sin4ψ = log sin33°46'20" - 51320.9 (1.6312"), giving 9.74498 58212.1.
- log|sin7ψ| = log sin75°54'0" - 11357.7 (2.1475"), giving 9.98671 32925.3.

Auxiliary column: 9.3233592 plus log cot 9.5532702, 0.1747472 and 9.3999970; logs of 3, 4, 7 are added for the factor k.

Logarithms entering the solution:
- log(sin3ψ/6) = 9.19573 36609.9, with u-term -0.2258139u.
- log sin4ψ = 9.74498 58212.1, with u-term -1.2594078u.
- log(|sin7ψ|/3) = 9.50959 20378.1, with u-term +0.3702152u.

Differences:
- 7 log r = 0.54925 21602.2 - 1.0335939u
- 4 log r = 0.31385 83768.2 + 0.5960291u
- 3 log r = 0.23539 37834.0 - 1.6296230u

Dividing by 7, 4 and 3:
- 0.07846 45943.2 - 0.1476563u
- 0.07846 45942.0 + 0.149007u (written 0.1480073)
- 0.07846 45944.7 - 0.5432077u

Solution:
- Equating the 7- and 3-equations gives u = +0.0000379".
- Then log r = 0.07846 45942.6, so r ≈ 1.19803.
- ψ = 36°33'25.4075379", so the root's argument is 143°26'34.5925".

CONSISTENCY CHECK (mine). The x^6 coefficient is 0, so the seven roots sum to zero. Using 1.5819 + 2[1.09748 cos47.755° + 1.48125 cos112.483° + 1.19803 cos143.443°] ≈ 0, which checks.

The next page applies Graeffe root-squaring to the same polynomial (as x^7 + 3x^4 + 6) to get the moduli independently.
errors: Part 2: the quotient of the 4 log r coefficient, 0.5960291/4 = 0.1490073, is written 0.14800 73 (slip in the third digit). It is harmless because u was found from the 7- and 3-equations only. With the correct value the 4-equation gives 45942.56 at the final u, consistent with 45942.6.
Equation 2 against equation 3 would give u ≈ 3.90e-5 rather than 3.79e-5. This is a rounding-level discrepancy of about 0.1 unit in the 10th log place, not an error.
The final φ of Part 1 (47°45'19.1926365") is not written out; only u = -0.0000116 is given.
No substantive errors otherwise: all angle multiplications, log subtractions, divisions and derivative coefficients check to the last digit.

results.what: Computation of complex roots of the trinomial x^7 - 3x^4 - 6 = 0 in polar form. Real and imaginary parts give r^7 = -6 sin4φ/sin3φ and r^4 = -2 sin7φ/sin3φ; φ is adjusted until the values of log r from 7 log r, 4 log r and 3 log r coincide.
results.modern_name: Polar (modulus–argument) solution of trinomial equations; a Newton-type correction in the argument using logarithmic differentials
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, 'Beiträge zur Theorie der algebraischen Gleichungen' (1849), which treats trinomials x^(m+n) + a x^m + b = 0 this way (worked example x^7 - 28x^4 + 480 = 0, to my recollection)

results.what: Linear correction of tabular log-sines via d log sin x = M cot x dx·sin1'', used to set up a linear equation for the correction u
results.modern_name: Linear interpolation / first-order differential correction (Newton's method)

results.what: Numerical complex roots: r ≈ 1.09748 at arg 47°45'19.19"; r ≈ 1.19803 at arg 143°26'34.59" (together with the earlier 112°29' pair and the real root ≈ 1.5819)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a high-precision worked example of the polar method for trinomial equations that Gauss published in 1849. The next page's Graeffe-type root squaring is also a known Gauss interest. It is new only as an unpublished numerical example.
